topic.title: Physics-Informed Learning and Differential-Equation Solvers
topic.area: Continuous Models and Scientific Machine Learning
topic.overview: Physics-informed methods incorporate differential equations or simulators into learning objectives and architectures. This cluster examines neural PDE solvers, differentiable physics, operator approximation, and training failures caused by conditioning or discretization. Encoding a correct equation is only one part of obtaining an accurate numerical solution.
topic.whyItMatters: A network may be expressive enough to represent a physical solution yet fail because its loss is difficult to optimize. Numerical bias, derivative cost, and multiscale structure must be considered alongside the chosen neural architecture.
topic.evolution: The collection includes early physical-model ideas and later PDE discovery and differentiable simulation. Recent work characterizes PINN failures and introduces curricula, solver-in-the-loop training, and specialized optimizers. The newest examples study test-time operator splitting and unbiased stochastic PDE objectives that avoid expensive second derivatives.
openQuestions: How can optimization failure be distinguished from insufficient physical information?
Which discretization guarantees remain meaningful when the solution model is learned?
